items.followUp: What is the purpose of the <head> section in an HTML document?

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies the body tags.
rubric.description: Identifies the opening and closing body tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming <body> and </body>.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of what the body section contains.
rubric.description: States that the body contains the content displayed on the webpage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the purpose of the body section.

modelAnswer: The body section is the part of an HTML document enclosed between the <body> and </body> tags.
It contains the webpage content that is displayed in the browser.

items.followUp: Write HTML code to display a paragraph and a level-two heading.

rubric.why: Checks correct use of HTML heading tags.
rubric.description: States that headings use the <h1> to <h6> tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the heading-tag range.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of heading levels.
rubric.description: Explains that <h1> is the largest heading and <h6> is the smallest.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the relative heading sizes.

modelAnswer: HTML headings and sub-headings are written using the <h1> to <h6> tags.
<h1> is the largest heading and <h6> is the smallest.

Example:

Main Heading

and

Sub-heading

.

items.followUp: Name and explain two other common flowchart symbols.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the start/end symbol.
rubric.description: Explains that the oval or terminator represents the start or end of a flowchart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct symbol and its use.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the process symbol.
rubric.description: Explains that a rectangle represents a processing step or instruction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct symbol and its use.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the input/output symbol.
rubric.description: Explains that a parallelogram represents input or output of data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct symbol and its use.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the decision symbol.
rubric.description: Explains that a diamond represents a condition with alternative branches, such as Yes/No.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct symbol and its use.

modelAnswer: 1. Terminal (oval): It shows the beginning or end of a flowchart.
2. Process (rectangle): It represents an operation, calculation, or instruction.
3. Input/Output (parallelogram): It represents data entering or leaving the system.
4. Decision (diamond): It represents a condition and branches, for example, into Yes and No paths.

items.followUp: What information does a router use to forward a data packet?

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies the destination information used in routing.
rubric.description: States that the router examines the packet's destination network or IP address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the destination address.

rubric.why: Checks that the student knows how a route is selected.
rubric.description: Explains that the router consults its routing table to select a suitable or best route.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the routing table and route selection.

rubric.why: Checks the forwarding step.
rubric.description: States that the packet is forwarded to the next router or outgoing interface on the selected route.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing forwarding.

rubric.why: Checks understanding that routing continues across networks.
rubric.description: Explains that routers repeat this process until the packet reaches its destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the repeated process or delivery.

modelAnswer: Routing is the process of choosing a path for data packets to travel from a source network to a destination network.
A router examines the destination IP address in a packet and consults its routing table.
It selects the best available route and forwards the packet to the next router or outgoing interface.
Routers repeat this process until the packet reaches the destination network.

items.followUp: What is a digital certificate, and how does it help protect a website connection?

rubric.why: Checks the basic meaning of encryption.
rubric.description: Defines encryption as changing readable data into an unreadable form using a key or method.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Checks that the student explains how the information can be recovered or accessed.
rubric.description: States that the data can be decrypted or read by someone with the correct key.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining key-based access or decryption.

rubric.why: Checks the everyday importance of protecting online information.
rubric.description: Explains that encryption helps protect personal or sensitive information sent over the internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant privacy or security benefit.

rubric.why: Checks application of encryption to daily internet use.
rubric.description: Gives a valid everyday example, such as online banking, passwords, payments, or private messages.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one suitable example.

modelAnswer: Encryption is the process of converting readable data into an unreadable form so that unauthorized people cannot understand it.
The data can be changed back into readable form by decryption using the correct key.
Encryption protects sensitive information sent over the internet, such as passwords and banking details.
It helps keep online banking, shopping payments, and private messages secure from unauthorized access.

items.followUp: What information should be identified when analysing a problem before writing a program?

rubric.why: Checks that the student begins by identifying and understanding the problem.
rubric.description: States that the problem must first be identified and understood clearly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying or understanding the problem.

rubric.why: Checks that the student considers what the problem requires and what information it uses or produces.
rubric.description: States that requirements, inputs, outputs, or constraints should be determined.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming relevant problem requirements or information.

modelAnswer: First, identify the problem and understand exactly what needs to be solved.
Then determine its requirements, including the inputs, expected outputs, and any constraints.

items.followUp: Explain why identifying the inputs and outputs is important in problem analysis.

rubric.why: Checks the central purpose of problem analysis.
rubric.description: Defines problem analysis as carefully examining and understanding a problem before solving it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the idea of examining or understanding the problem.

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies the elements considered during analysis.
rubric.description: Mentions determining the problem's inputs, processing requirements, and/or expected outputs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying relevant elements of the analysis.

modelAnswer: Problem Analysis is the process of carefully examining and understanding a problem before developing its solution.
It includes identifying the required inputs, the processing needed, and the expected outputs.

items.followUp: Write the basic structure of an HTML document and label its sections.

rubric.why: Checks that the student names the document's head section.
rubric.description: Names the head section as a main section of an HTML document.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming head.

rubric.why: Checks that the student names the document's body section.
rubric.description: Names the body section as a main section of an HTML document.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming body.

modelAnswer: The two main sections of an HTML document are the head section and the body section.
They are written using the <head>...</head> and <body>...</body> tags, within the outer <html>...</html> element.
